judged_text: In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` can never match because it only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find predicate compares against null/undefined and always returns undefined. When EventManager.update calls updateEvent with a null externalCalendarId (calendarReference found without externalCalendarId), selectedCalendar is undefined, calendar.events.update is invoked with calendarId undefined, and Google returns 'Missing required query parameter calendarId' — reschedule updates that previously fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId now fail and the calendar event is silently left stale.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
Because this branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null/undefined/""`), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` against a falsy value, so it will almost always return `undefined` and does not actually “fall back” to any destination calendar. The same pattern exists in `deleteEvent`.

Separately in `EventManager.update...` the code explicitly sets `calenderExternalId` to `null` when the reference has no `externalCalendarId`, and passes that through to `updateEvent(...)`, so the buggy fallback is reachable from this diff. This can lead to passing an undefined/invalid `calendarId` to Google’s API or updating the wrong calendar (e.g., not the intended destination calendar).
